resources.string: The app will intercept and log your HTTPS traffic so you can inspect every request and response on this device.\n\nAfter you confirm, the app will ask you to install a CA certificate. This is required to decrypt HTTPS. The certificate stays on your device and can be removed at any time from Settings → Security → Certificates.

Android requires a screen lock (PIN, pattern or password) before installing CA certificates.

Go to:
Settings → Security → Screen lock

Set a PIN or password, then come back and tap Install.

Android 11 and newer only allow CA certificates to be installed from the Settings app, not from inside other apps.

The certificate was saved to Downloads as:
%1$s

1. Tap Open Settings (it opens “Install a certificate”)
2. Tap CA certificate → Install anyway
3. Open Download and pick %1$s. Older privacyguard_ca files there are from earlier installs and no longer work.
4. Come back here: the card turns green once Android trusts it.

If Settings opens a different page, search Settings for “CA certificate”.
The certificate could not be written to Downloads. Check free storage and try again; details are in logcat under the CaInstallHelper tag.
Inspection is off and the signing key has been deleted, but Android still trusts the installed CA. Remove it in Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → User credentials.
Install the CA, then test with a browser. Apps using pinning, QUIC/UDP or end-to-end encryption may show metadata only.
Turn on the switch above to start.
UDP/443 is being dropped. Chrome, YouTube and WhatsApp fall back to TLS/TCP and can be inspected.
Turn on to drop UDP/443 (QUIC), so apps retry over TLS/TCP. Needed to inspect Chrome and YouTube traffic.
Install the CA certificate to decrypt HTTPS

Browsers that trust user certificates (Chrome, Edge, Brave) now show full payloads. Most other apps ignore user-installed CAs since Android 7, and pinned apps (WhatsApp, Instagram, banking) always show metadata only. That\'s an Android limit, not a bug.
Tap Regenerate to try again. If the problem persists, clear the app\'s storage in Android Settings and reopen the app.
Tap Install. Android asks you to name the certificate: type anything and tap OK.
Android 11+ only installs CA certificates from Settings. Tap Install: the certificate is saved to Downloads and you\'ll get step-by-step instructions.
Generating the CA for the first time. This takes a few seconds.
